Economy rules

Rarity drives value first. Flagship bulk base cards use a flatter £0.50–£1 sell range and unnumbered common inserts only sit slightly above them. Numbered versions keep the stronger scarcity model. Sapphire remains the premium gamble: bulk stays modest, while numbered Sapphire cards carry a very large premium so the four guaranteed Hobby numbereds create a stronger floor without making base cards profitable. Flagship Value now leans heavily toward /50 and /25; /10, /5 and 1/1 are substantially harder there, making Hobby the better route to low-numbered Flagship cards. Sapphire autos remain modestly increased. Selling is still locked in this test build.

Base vs regular insert

For the same player and serial number, a base parallel gets a 25% premium over an ordinary insert parallel. True chase inserts are excluded because their own pack odds determine their value.

Recovery Mode

Complete objectives using temporary 5-card UCC Flagship packs. Recovery cards never enter your collection and cannot be sold or exchanged. Objectives overlap, so every pack can progress several at once.
Easy £10 · Medium £15 · Hard £30 · Finish all five for a £20 completion bonus. A normal full run should take roughly 20–40 packs.
